issues.body:
`grep -rn 'role-labels\|ROLE_LABELS' . --exclude-dir=.git` returns hits ONLY inside scripts/triage.py: the definition (49), the `_role()` gate (237), one self-test (669), the argparse flag (1243) and the printer (1263). No workflow, script, shell helper or scripts/selftest-suite.txt entry invokes `--role-labels`, and nothing in the repo runs `gh label create`.

This is a merge artifact. Round 1 reviewed a version of .github/workflows/triage-issue.yml that consumed `--role-labels` in a `gh label create` reconcile loop parsed with `IFS=$'\t'`. The merge in 85c39b8f ('merge master into #593 to resolve conflicts') took master's refactor, which applies the plan via `python3 scripts/triage.py --apply` (triage-issue.yml:95) with an in-Python fail-closed applier. The reconcile loop is gone; the flag it existed to feed was left behind.

Two consequences. (1) The `(color, description)` tuples are entirely dead data -- no code path ever reads them, so the catalog's only live role is as a membership set, for which the colors and descriptions are noise. (2) The flag's help text calls this 'the canonical role-label catalog', which reads as a promise that the repo's role labels are reconciled from here. They are not. A maintainer who adds a role to ROLE_LABELS expecting the label to be created will get a silently unreconciled repo -- and, because of the gate at line 237, a behavioural change they did not ask for.

This is the diff's central artifact, so its stated benefit is entirely unrealized while the behavioural risk it justifies is live.
issues.fix_hint: Decide which half of this change you actually want. If the catalog is meant to reconcile labels, restore a consumer -- and prefer doing it in Python inside the existing `--apply` path (which already reads the live set via `repo_label_set`) over reintroducing a shell loop, so the failure is observed by an exception rather than by errexit. If reconciliation is out of scope for this PR, drop `--role-labels`, the printer and the color/description payload, and reduce the catalog to the plain set it is actually used as (`ROLE_LABELS = frozenset({...})`) -- or drop it entirely per the next issue.
issues.title: `--role-labels` and the ROLE_LABELS color/description payload have no consumer anywhere in the repo

issues.fix_hint: Prefer deleting the gate and letting the existing known_labels check own this: it is live-data-driven, already fail-closed, preserves a valid incumbent role, and explains itself. If you keep a static gate, it must not be silent or pre-emptive -- move it inside the `if role:` branch so it appends the same style of warning and reuses the `keep = sorted(existing)` preservation, and assert `{f'role:{k}' for k in ROLE_LABELS} == {lb for lb in REAL if lb.startswith('role:')}` so the literal cannot drift from the pinned live set (see the next issue).
issues.title: New `_role()` gate silently demotes an explicit role, pre-empting the #582 warn-and-preserve path and duplicating the live label-set authority

issues.body:
The fixture is `{"role:impl", "area:worker", "priority:P2", "from:agent"}`. SEC_KEYWORDS (line 121) contains "worker", which substring-matches `area:worker`, so `_role()` short-circuits to TRUST_PLANE_ROLE on its FIRST statement -- before the explicit-role branch this diff modified. Both checks therefore evaluate identically on pre-diff and post-diff code and cannot flip red on this change. The comment calling them an 'Exact regression' overstates what they pin.

Worse, round 1 flagged this and the response was to rewrite the expectation rather than the test. With TRUST_PLANE_ROLE == "impl" and the incumbent already `role:impl`, the target is already present, so `add - labels` drops it and remove is empty. The assertion is now literally `(False, False)` -- i.e. it asserts that NOTHING is added and NOTHING is removed -- under the name 'adds before remove'. The name claims an ordering guarantee; the body asserts the absence of both operations. Nothing here touches ordering at all (ordering is enforced by apply_triage's phased sequence, which these lines never invoke).

`trust role replacement is exactly-one` is a genuine invariant and worth keeping, but it too is unchanged by this diff.

Note `unknown explicit role rejected` (line 670) IS non-vacuous -- it returns "not-a-repo-label" on pre-diff code -- so the gate mechanism itself is covered. What is missing is coverage of the gate on a path where it is actually reachable in anger.
issues.fix_hint: Rename to `trust role replacement plans no churn when the target is already present`, matching what it asserts. Then add a case that actually exercises the changed branch: an explicit role on a NON-trust area, so SEC_KEYWORDS does not short-circuit -- e.g. `_role(["role:soundness", "area:docs"], "task")`. Assert both the returned role AND that a warning was emitted, so the silent-demotion behaviour in the issue above is pinned one way or the other. For real ordering coverage, drive apply_triage against the existing FakeGh rather than inspecting plan sets.
issues.title: `trust role replacement adds before remove` asserts no ordering and now asserts a no-op; both trust-replacement checks are vacuous for this diff

issues.body:
Two gaps.

(1) Wrong branch. `derived_roles` is built from ROLE_BY_KIND, ROLE_BY_TYPE, the UI/INFRA surface labels and area:dispatch -- all DERIVATION paths, none of which this diff touched. It evaluates to {docs, research, ci, site, impl}, exactly set(ROLE_LABELS), so it passes. It is structurally incapable of exercising the explicit-role gate the diff added, because no derivation can produce a role outside the catalog.

(2) Incomplete producer set. It omits `AREA_ROLE_DEFAULT.values()`, which the comment at line 854 explicitly identifies as 'a THIRD producer of role labels'. The pre-existing check at 858-861 correctly includes it when testing against REAL; the new check does not when testing against ROLE_LABELS. Harmless today (those values are {impl, ci, site, docs}) and the REAL check would still catch a bad entry, but the asymmetry between two adjacent checks over the same question is a trap.

(3) The check that would actually matter is absent. This file now carries TWO hand-maintained literals both claiming to enumerate the registry's role labels: ROLE_LABELS (49) and REAL (838, pinned from `gh label list`). They agree today. Nothing asserts they agree. Since ROLE_LABELS is documented as the catalog labels would be created from, a future entry added there but not to REAL would make REAL's 'live label set' comment silently false -- and vice versa a role added to REAL but not ROLE_LABELS becomes unusable via the new gate with no test going red.
issues.fix_hint: Add `chk("catalog == the pinned live role labels", {f"role:{k}" for k in ROLE_LABELS}, {lb for lb in REAL if lb.startswith("role:")})`. That single assertion is the drift check that matters and it subsumes most of the intent here. Also fold `set(AREA_ROLE_DEFAULT.values())` into `derived_roles` so it matches the producer set the neighbouring check at 858 already uses. Keep the derived-roles check as a separate invariant.
issues.title: `all derived roles have labels` covers the unchanged branch, omits AREA_ROLE_DEFAULT, and nothing binds ROLE_LABELS to the pinned REAL set

issues.body:
The printer emits `f"role:{role}\t{color}\t{description}"`. Round 1 raised this against a workflow that parsed it with `IFS=$'\t' read -r label color description`; that consumer no longer exists (see the first issue), so there is currently no cross-file contract to break. Recording it because the moment a consumer is restored, the TAB-separated one-record-per-line shape and the `role:` prefix become load-bearing again, and `_self_test` asserts only on ROLE_LABELS as a dict -- a description gaining a tab or newline would break the consumer with nothing red in the gate.

Also cosmetic, and not worth its own issue: the diff removes the blank line at old line 105, which visually welds the new ROLE_LABELS block onto the TRUST-PLANE comment banner it is unrelated to. And the `[OPUS-4.8]` markers were removed from both file headers while `[OPUS-5]`, `[FABLE-5]` and similar markers remain inline throughout scripts/triage.py, so the provenance cleanup is inconsistent -- fine if that is a staged sweep, worth stating in the PR description if so.
issues.fix_hint: If you keep the flag and give it a consumer, add a check that renders the catalog the way main() does and asserts each line splits into exactly 3 TAB fields, the first starts with `role:`, and no field contains a tab or newline. If you drop the flag per the first issue, this disappears with it. Restore the blank line above ROLE_LABELS either way.
issues.title: `--role-labels` output shape is untested

verdict.summary:
The two model-marker header removals are correct and match the model-agnostic provenance rule. On the substance, I have to correct round 1 rather than repeat it: its blocker does NOT hold. scripts/triage.py:838 already pins REAL, the registry's live label set (gh label list, 2026-07-25), and it confirms role:review and role:soundness do NOT exist in this repository -- routing.toml carries those routes deliberately as forward-looking config (line 92's TODO says so). ROLE_LABELS' five entries are exactly REAL's role subset, so the catalog is in sync and the 'review lane starves' claim is unfounded. Round 1's two workflow findings are also moot: the merge in 85c39b8f replaced the shell reconcile loop with `--apply`, so the `|| true` and process-substitution concerns no longer exist.

That merge is also what breaks this diff. `--role-labels` and the entire (color, description) payload now have ZERO consumers: grep over the whole repo returns hits only inside scripts/triage.py itself (lines 49, 237, 669, 1243, 1263). Nothing calls `gh label create`; triage-issue.yml:95 goes straight to `--apply`. So the diff ships a CLI surface documented as 'the canonical role-label catalog' that never creates a label, while the behavioural half of it -- the `_role()` gate -- does land. That gate is the second problem: triage() already receives the LIVE label set (`known = repo_label_set(repo)`, line 566) and already has a fail-closed path for a missing role label that KEEPS the incumbent role and emits a loud warning. The new gate pre-empts that path with a hard-coded literal, returns None, and emits NO warning -- a silent demotion to status:untriaged where the existing mechanism would have preserved a valid role and said why. It fails closed and retriage can recover status:untriaged, so this is major, not a blocker.

Round 1's test findings (#2 self-test scope, #4 vacuity, #6 output contract) are untouched, and #4 regressed into an actively misleading assertion.… [truncated 110 chars]
